bull.t: AMP immunotherapy platform and oncology pipeline
bull.b: The AMP platform gives Elicio a defined technological approach for directing immune-stimulating agents and antigens to lymph nodes. Its application across pancreatic cancer and other solid tumors could support a broader development strategy if clinical testing validates stronger tumor-specific T-cell responses.

Leverage has improved substantially from the highly elevated 2025 level, reducing immediate balance-sheet pressure and improving financial flexibility relative to the prior year. This is a meaningful structural improvement, although continued losses could still erode the capital base without further financing.

The reduction in annual net losses over the last reported periods indicates some improvement in expense or development-spending intensity, even though profitability remains distant. If maintained, lower losses could extend the company’s financial runway and make future funding needs more manageable.

bear.t: No revenue or commercial operating base
bear.b: Elicio has not yet established revenue generation, leaving the business dependent on clinical progress and external capital rather than customer-funded operations. Until a program reaches commercialization, the company lacks operating leverage and remains exposed to delays, trial outcomes, and financing requirements.

Sustained cash consumption at roughly $37.7M annually places continuing pressure on liquidity and capital allocation. Because the burn has not meaningfully improved, Elicio may need repeated financing to maintain development activity, potentially limiting strategic flexibility and increasing dilution exposure.

bear.t: Phase 2 trial missed its primary endpoint
bear.b: Missing the primary endpoint is a material validation and execution risk for the clinical pipeline, because post-hoc subgroup observations are less definitive than the prespecified result. The setback can lengthen development timelines, require additional evidence, and increase the capital needed before potential approval.
